title: ConfigEffectiveOutput
description: The resolved-configuration report `duckduckgo-search-cli config effective` writes on stdout. Where `config list` reports only what is STORED, this reports what would actually APPLY, showing each layer separately so a caller can see why. Carries no `type` discriminator; identified by the subcommand invoked. Added in v1.0.3 (GAP-SCHEMA-INTROSPECTION-UNDECLARED-001). English-only: configuration key names are part of the CLI contract.

type.description: Envelope discriminator (v1.0.4+). Emitted by `types::ConfigKind::ConfigEffective`, a compiler-checked constant rather than a hand-typed literal.

allowed_keys.description: Every key `config set` accepts. A key absent here is rejected.

note.description: Why the `cli` layer is always null in this report: `config effective` takes no search flags, so there is no CLI layer to resolve. At runtime a search DOES apply CLI over XDG over default.

precedence.description: The resolution order, strongest first. Published as data so a caller reasoning about `source` does not have to hardcode the rule.

values.description: One entry per key in `allowed_keys`, showing each layer and the winner.

cli.description: Always null in this report — see the top-level `note`. Present rather than omitted so the layer table has a uniform shape.

xdg.description: Value stored in `config.toml`, or null when unset.

default.description: Compiled-in default, or null when the knob has none.

effective.description: The value that would actually apply. Null means the knob is genuinely unset and has no default.

source.description: Which layer won. Never `cli` here, because this report resolves no CLI flags.
